title: "Solutions: Extra practice: logistic regression"

::: {.callout-note}
These are the solutions to the
[Extra practice: logistic regression](../lecture-02/09-practice-logistic-regression.qmd) exercises.
Try each exercise yourself before you look.
:::

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(medicaldata)
```

`blood` and `cmv`, made at the top of the exercise page:

```{r}
blood <- blood_storage |>
  mutate(
    recurrence = factor(Recurrence, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    rbc_age_group = factor(RBC.Age.Group, levels = 1:3,
                           labels = c("younger", "middle", "older"))
  )

cmv <- cytomegalovirus |>
  mutate(
    cmv = factor(cmv, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    recipient.cmv = factor(recipient.cmv, levels = c(0, 1),
                           labels = c("negative", "positive")),
    donor.cmv = factor(donor.cmv, levels = c(0, 1),
                       labels = c("negative", "positive"))
  )
```

## Exercise 1: Adjust for other risk factors

```{r}
rec_fit_adj <- logistic_reg() |>
  fit(recurrence ~ rbc_age_group + Age + PVol + PreopPSA + factor(TVol),
      data = blood)

rec_or <- tidy(rec_fit_adj, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
rec_or
```

```{r}
blood |>
  summarize(across(c(Age, PVol, PreopPSA, TVol), \(x) sum(is.na(x))))
```

- `glm()` drops rows with missing `PVol`, `PreopPSA` or `TVol`.
- Storage age still shows no association.
- Each 1 ng/mL of preoperative PSA multiplies the odds of recurrence by
  `r round(rec_or$estimate[rec_or$term == "PreopPSA"], 2)`
  (95% CI `r round(rec_or$conf.low[rec_or$term == "PreopPSA"], 2)`
  to `r round(rec_or$conf.high[rec_or$term == "PreopPSA"], 2)`).
- Larger tumour volumes (`TVol` 2 and 3, compared with 1)
  have much higher odds of recurrence,
  but very wide confidence intervals:
  few men in the lowest tumour-volume group had a recurrence.

```{r}
blood |>
  count(TVol, recurrence)
```

## Exercise 2: Plot the odds ratios

```{r}
#| warning: false
rec_or |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Odds ratio (log scale, 95% CI)", y = NULL)
```

## Exercise 3: The same as `glm()`

```{r}
glm(recurrence ~ rbc_age_group, data = blood, family = binomial) |>
  tidy(exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)

logistic_reg() |>
  fit(recurrence ~ rbc_age_group, data = blood) |>
  tidy(exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
```

The same odds ratios:
`logistic_reg()` uses `glm()` underneath.

## Exercise 4: What does this model ignore?

Time.
The men were followed for different lengths of time
(`TimeToRecurrence`),
and some left the study before a recurrence could be seen
(`Censor`).
Logistic regression only asks *whether* recurrence happened;
survival analysis, as the original study used,
also models *when*.

## Exercise 5: Cytomegalovirus

```{r}
cmv_fit <- logistic_reg() |>
  fit(cmv ~ donor.cmv + recipient.cmv + time.to.transplant, data = cmv)

cmv_or <- tidy(cmv_fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
cmv_or
```

A CMV-positive recipient has
`r round(cmv_or$estimate[cmv_or$term == "recipient.cmvpositive"], 1)` times the odds of reactivation
(95% CI `r round(cmv_or$conf.low[cmv_or$term == "recipient.cmvpositive"], 1)`
to `r round(cmv_or$conf.high[cmv_or$term == "recipient.cmvpositive"], 1)`).
With only 64 patients, every interval is wide.
